question: Explanation
options: A) Drop any performance note written before the current review year, using only recent evidence.
B) Tell the candidates that AI was used to prepare the summaries the promotion panel will be reading.
C) Examine whether the rankings systematically disadvantage any group before the panel relies on them.
D) Have Claude state a confidence score for each ranking so that the panel can see which ones are shakiest.
E) Include only those candidates who actively agree to have their own notes summarised by Claude at all.
correct_answers: B) Tell the candidates that AI was used to prepare the summaries the promotion panel will be reading.
C) Examine whether the rankings systematically disadvantage any group before the panel relies on them.
explanations: Restricting the time window changes the evidence base but says nothing about whether the ranking treats groups equally.
Correct on independent grounds: people affected by a decision are owed transparency about how their case was prepared.
Correct. Performance notes carry human bias, and a ranking built on them can reproduce that bias at scale unless it is checked.
A self-reported confidence score is not a reliable measure of correctness and does not reveal systematic unfairness.
Opting out of a promotion process is not a real choice for candidates and would itself create unequal treatment.
